limitations: Native directory-picker UI was not exercised; browser integration supplied a picker result through a test-only Rust protocol adapter.
Windows/Linux directory core passed cross-compilation checks but was not executed on those platforms.
No host installer was built, installed, published or substituted for the current application.
OS-sandbox distributions require persistent bookmark/token/portal adapters before enabling this capability.

scenarios: reload with persistent grant no SQL
failed commit preserves all files byte for byte
restore real files after host restart
field name and comment search from cache
whole database Markdown export from cache
real host revocation persists after reload without UI preferences
never falls back to an older grant
reauthorization restores original files with no SQL or file changes

failureCoverage: Interrupted writes and checksum failures preserve prior committed file (Rust core).
Revoke/changed identity/unavailable root deny access without recreating the root.
Read-only and cross-plugin handle access denied.
Failed preference persistence and interrupted directory switch retain the previous selected directory.
Full UI storage and missing UI preferences still restore the host-selected directory.
Browser-injected commit failure preserves every snapshot byte and successful sync timestamp.
Conflicting writes fail without replacing the existing file.
Legacy UI/native cache migration leaves original copies intact.
